questions.q:
Column-I gives pair of curves and column-II gives the angle $\theta$ between the curves at their intersection point.

\begin{array}{|l|l|}
\hline
\text{\textbf{Column-I}} & \text{\textbf{Column-II}} \\
\hline
\text{(A)} y = \sin x, y = \cos x & \text{(P)} \frac{\pi}{4} \\
\text{(B)} x^2 = 4y, y = \frac{8}{x^2+4} & \text{(Q)} \frac{\pi}{2} \\
\text{(C)} \frac{x^2}{18} + \frac{y^2}{8} = 1, x^2 - y^2 = 5 & \text{(R)} \tan^{-1} 3 \\
\text{(D)} xy = 1, x^2 - y^2 = 5 & \text{(S)} \tan^{-1} 5 \\
 & \text{(T)} \tan^{-1}(2\sqrt{2}) \\
\hline
\end{array}

 & \text{(T) Indeterminate} \\

Let $f(x) = \frac{x^3 - 4}{(x-1)^3} \forall x \neq 1, g(x) = \frac{x^4 - 2x^2}{4} \forall x \in \mathbb{R}, h(x) = \frac{x^3 + 4}{(x+1)^3} \forall x \neq -1$,

\begin{array}{|l|l|}
\hline
\text{\textbf{Column-I}} & \text{\textbf{Column-II}} \\
\hline
\text{(A) The number of possible distinct real roots of equation} f(x) = c \text{where} c \ge 4 \text{can be} & \text{(P) 0} \\
\text{(B) The number of possible distinct real roots of equation} g(x) = c \text{, where} c \ge 0 \text{can be} & \text{(Q) 1} \\
\text{(C) The number of possible distinct real roots of equation} h(x) = c \text{, where} c \ge 1 \text{can be} & \text{(R) 2} \\
\text{(D) The number of possible distinct real roots of equation} g(x) = c \text{where} -1 < c < 0 \text{can be} & \text{(S) 3} \\
 & \text{(T) 4} \\
\hline
\end{array}

\text{(B) If} x^3 + ax + 1 = 0 \text{and} x^4 + ax + 1 = 0 \text{have a common roots then the value of} |a| \text{can be equal to} & \text{(Q) 3} \\

\text{(D) If} f(x) = 2|x|^3 + 3x^2 - 12|x| + 1 \text{, where} x \in [-1, 2] \text{then greatest value of} f(x) \text{is more than} & \text{(S) 5} \\

questions.q:
Consider the function $f(x) = \frac{\ln x}{8} - ax + x^2$ and $a \ge 0$ is a real constant :

\begin{array}{|l|l|}
\hline
\text{\textbf{Column-I}} & \text{\textbf{Column-II}} \\
\hline
\text{(A)} f(x) \text{gives a local maxima at} & \text{(P)} a = 1; x = \frac{1}{4} \\
\text{(B)} f(x) \text{gives a local minima at} & \text{(Q)} a > 1; x = \frac{a - \sqrt{a^2 - 1}}{4} \\
\text{(C)} f(x) \text{gives a point of inflection for} & \text{(R)} 0 \le a < 1 \\
\text{(D)} f(x) \text{is strictly increasing for all} x \in \mathbb{R}^+ & \text{(S)} a > 1; x = \frac{a + \sqrt{a^2 - 1}}{4} \\
\hline
\end{array}
questions.source: Black Book · Application of Derivatives · Exercise 4: Matrix Match Type Problems · Q6

The function $f(x) = \sqrt{ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d}$ has its non-zero local minimum and maximum values at $x = -2$ and $x = 2$ respectively. If '$a$' is one of the root of $x^2 - x - 6 = 0$, then match the following :

\begin{array}{|l|l|}
\hline
\text{\textbf{Column-I}} & \text{\textbf{Column-II}} \\
\hline
\text{(A) The value of '} a \text{' is} & \text{(P) 0} \\
\text{(B) The value of '} b \text{' is} & \text{(Q) 24} \\
\text{(C) The value of '} c \text{' is} & \text{(R) Greater than 32} \\
\text{(D) The value of '} d \text{' is} & \text{(S) -2} \\
\hline
\end{array}
